text: It's far better to buy a wonderful company at a fair price than a fair company at a wonderful price.
context: The lesson he says Charlie Munger understood early and he learned slowly, after the cigar-butt years.

text: Time is the friend of the wonderful business, the enemy of the mediocre.
context: Why a cheap price on a poor business disappoints: the low return eats the bargain.

text: In a difficult business, no sooner is one problem solved than another surfaces — never is there just one cockroach in the kitchen.
context: His warning that a bargain price in a hard business is rarely the only problem.

text: When a management with a reputation for brilliance tackles a business with a reputation for bad economics, it is the reputation of the business that remains intact.
context: Able people at Berkshire's textile business and at Hochschild Kohn could not outrun quicksand.

text: When we own portions of outstanding businesses with outstanding managements, our favorite holding period is forever.
context: Written about Coca-Cola and Freddie Mac. He contrasts it with cutting the flowers and watering the weeds.

text: Our goal is more modest: we simply attempt to be fearful when others are greedy and to be greedy only when others are fearful.
context: He calls fear and greed super-contagious diseases whose timing he does not try to predict.

text: The difference between GEICO's costs and those of its competitors is a kind of moat that protects a valuable and much-sought-after business castle.
context: His early moat image: low costs as the water around an economic franchise.

text: You only have to be able to evaluate companies within your circle of competence. The size of that circle is not very important; knowing its boundaries, however, is vital.
context: Advice for shareholders who build their own portfolios instead of buying a low-fee index fund.

text: If you aren't willing to own a stock for ten years, don't even think about owning it for ten minutes.
context: The temptation he tells investors to resist once a business meets the test.

text: Intelligent investing is not complex, though that is far from saying that it is easy.
context: The setup for his claim that two courses matter: how to value a business, and how to think about market prices.

text: The stock market serves as a relocation center at which money is moved from the active to the patient.
context: His account of Berkshire's stay-put holdings. The popular shorter line about the impatient and the patient is this sentence.

text: We can afford to lose money — even a lot of money. But we can't afford to lose reputation — even a shred of reputation.
context: The line he says he had already been sending managers for more than 25 years, reprinted with the July 26, 2010 memo in the 2010 Chairman's Letter.

text: Lose money for the firm, and I will be understanding. Lose a shred of reputation for the firm, and I will be ruthless.
context: Written as interim chairman after the Treasury-auction scandal, telling employees which loss he would not forgive.
